Rafael — attaching the initial evidence pack components. See the Drive link below for the full export and the CSV extracts. Deliverables included in this message:

Attachments (stubs):
- hsm_attestation_2026-05-31.pdf (PDF, vendor-signed attestation)

- operator_matrix_2026-06-15.xlsx (XLSX, roles and on-call schedule)
- kms_config_dump_lobscorp_anon.json (configuration dump, tenant ids replaced)

Quick answers to the SIG prompts (KMS/HSM section):
1) Custodianship model: Tenant data keys are encrypted with a tenant-specific KEK. KEKs are wrapped using our HSM cluster (Thales Luna SA) and access is restricted to the HSM operator role; Redwood holds the wrapping key material in hardware-protected keyslots.
2) Rotation cadence: KEKs are rotated on a quarterly cadence by default; critical keys (prod KEKs) also undergo emergency rotation procedures when suspicious activity is detected.
3) Wrap/unwrap process: Wrap operations occur inside the HSM; unwrap requires operator authorization + signed request logged in our audit system. We never unwrap to plaintext outside the HSM boundary.
4) Emergency rekey: Documented emergency rekey runbook exists; involves canary re-encryption, fallback routing to older key version for reads during rollover, and a validated re-encryption job. We can share an excerpt if the auditor needs it.

Notes/controls:
- Rotation logs are exported with operator IDs hashed (salted) for privacy; we can provide a redaction key under an NDA if Lobscorp requires de-anonymized operator traces for audit.
- The HSM attestation is vendor-signed and includes FIPS/TSP statuses.

Drive link (staged export): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/lobscorp/sig-evidence-2026 (internal access)
Jira ticket for this request: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4121
